one_line_contribution: A measurement claim plus intervention for agent-memory transfer: an LLM reader's own episode length (and therefore its served-token cost) is partly inherited from the number of steps in the retrieved item, so a self-collected on-policy pool costs the reader more than a short expert walkthrough at equal success, and deleting replay-verified no-op steps from a pool removes that inherited cost while adding them re-imposes it -- with the consequence that writers rank differently by gain-per-consumer-token than by success.
closest_prior_work: Three verified threats, none fatal. (1) 'The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory' (arXiv:2607.10608, verified via s2cli, S2 channel, 2026-07-12) is the closest in framing: it proposes a trajectory-level Enter-Propagation-Recovery analysis of exactly the question 'how does the retrieved item shape the reader's multi-step trajectory', and explicitly positions prior memory work as a supply-side literature that ignores consumption. It studies whether a wrong memory changes an action and propagates, i.e. the correctness axis; the proposal's length/cost axis is not in it. So it takes the framing sentence but not the claim -- the proposal must cite it and say what it adds, and it currently does not mention it at all. (2) AgentDiet (arXiv:2509.23586, verified, Proc. ACM Softw. Eng., 40 citations): trajectory reduction that removes 'waste' from the agent's execution to cut token cost without hurting success. This is the pruning half of P2 already demonstrated, but on the agent's own in-context history rather than on a retrieved foreign item, and with no writer-vs-reader relation. It makes 'pruning no-ops saves tokens at equal success' an expected result rather than a finding, which drains P2/P3 of surprise even if they are needed as controls. (3) SkillEvolBench (arXiv:2605.24117, verified) is the named antagonist for P2 (raw trajectories beat distilled skills because compression discards contextual cues) and the proposal handles it correctly. Also worth noting: 'What Demonstration Curation Metrics Do to Your Policy' (arXiv:2606.10229, verified) already concludes that 'any curation benchmark must control for episode length before reporting detection accuracy' -- the proposal cites this paper only for the defect-detection/policy decoupling result and misses that its own premise (demonstration length is the confound that matters) is already stated there for BC policies. Verified IDs: 2607.10608, 2509.23586, 2605.24117, 2512.02543 (returned under the retitle 'Inference-Time Distillation: Cost-Efficient Agents Without Fine-Tuning or Manual Prompt Engineering'), 2608.04003, 2606.24775, 2210.01379, 2606.10229, 2608.04843, 2608.07169 (verified via search listing, not the paper endpoint -- that endpoint timed out three times under rate limiting). Could not verify: 2608.31100 (S3Gym); 2604.14004, 2605.30723, 2606.01139 and the other brief-supplied ids were not checked as the novelty argument does not lean on them.
strongest_objection: The paper is two claims, and each fails a different way. The token half is accounting, not science: served tokens = injected tokens + prompt/completion tokens, and self-pool items are longer than expert walkthroughs by construction, so at matched success the expert pool wins on gain-per-served-token before the reader does anything. P4 -- the claim advertised as the payoff ('cost reranks writers') -- is therefore mostly a restatement of 'the self pool's items are longer', which the proposal itself measures in Preparation and logs as item lengths. The automated entailment check flags this as near-entailed and the proposal's answer (the auxiliary 8-net success-gap clause) resolves a different question. The step half, P1, is the genuinely open claim, but it is under-identified as designed: a reader taking more steps after being shown a longer item is consistent with at least three mechanisms -- copying the demonstrated path length (the proposal's account), being distracted by a longer, noisier prompt (a plain context-length effect that has nothing to do with step structure), and inferring from the exemplar that no-op and failed actions are normal behaviour (a policy-prior shift, not path copying). The only arm that separates path length from prompt length is the observation-truncation control, which runs at 2 seeds as a declared non-primary control, and truncating observation text is itself a content manipulation. Relatedly, 'content-preserving' is doing unearned work: inserting benign detours into a walkthrough changes the item's action distribution, and deleting every empty-state-diff step deletes exactly the examine/look steps that carry object-location information in ALFWorld -- replay-verification checks that a replayer still completes the task, which is not the same as checking that a reader can still find the object. So the headline slope, if it comes in at 0.4, will be reported as 'readers copy the writer's path' when the design cannot exclude 'longer prompts make readers flail'.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Promote the length-vs-tokens separation to a primary 4-seed arm and add the missing third cell: pad the expert walkthrough with the same number of *tokens* but no extra steps (e.g. verbose observation text, or a second unrelated walkthrough appended), so item steps and item tokens are crossed rather than merely truncated. A slope on steps that survives at fixed tokens, and a null slope on tokens at fixed steps, is the result that earns the title; without the crossing, P1 is a correlation between two things the manipulation moves together. (2) Rewrite P4 so it cannot be won by construction: pre-register the served-token gap implied by injected tokens alone (computable before any episode from the logged item lengths) and require the observed expert-vs-self ratio to exceed that construction-implied value, as the entailment check suggests; better, report the ratio with injected tokens held equal across writers. (3) Make P5(b) a TOST with a pre-registered equivalence band and enough seeds to bring the difference SE to ~0.10; as written a true self-recognition effect of 0.2 is confirmed as 'no effect' by a CI that is 0.33 wide, which is affirming the null. (4) Separate the two things the pruning rule conflates by scoring an information-preserving pruner (remove empty-diff steps whose observation text adds no new object-location fact) against the pure empty-diff rule; P2's outcome is currently a test of the ALFWorld state-diff heuristic as much as of the length claim. (5) Cite and position against arXiv:2607.10608 and arXiv:2509.23586 explicitly.
missing_baseline: The k knob, per writer. The plan cuts the k=1 cells ('carried no prediction'), but k is the cheapest and most obvious lever on consumer-side tokens, and Measurement C already gives the numbers that make it a live competitor: k1 - static3 = +9.1 at ~140 injected tokens versus k3 - static3 = +17.2 at ~430. Gain per served token for self-raw at k=1 may well exceed expert-at-k=3, in which case P4's 'writers rerank under cost' is really 'retrieve fewer items', and the recommended intervention (replay-verified pruning) is competing against a one-line config change it never runs against. A cost-axis paper that reports a per-token frontier over writers but not over k will be asked for this by every reviewer. Second, smaller omission in the same spirit: a one-sentence efficiency instruction ('reach the goal in as few actions as possible') appended to the k=3 expert or self-raw prompt -- the brief's own Appendix B rule is that the cheapest baseline runs first, and if a ~15-token instruction removes the inherited steps, the pruning pipeline has no practical claim left.
preprint_collision: No verified collision found; the central length-inheritance claim appears unclaimed, and the proposal's own check is one of the better ones I have seen in this round -- it names queries, channel and returned ids, runs the required home-literature query in imitation-learning vocabulary, and says for each hit why it misses. Queries I ran, all on the s2cli S2+HF channel (WebSearch unavailable in this session; no WebFetch): (a) 'retrieved demonstration length inherited reader episode length agent memory token cost' --recent -> Infini Memory 2606.10677, AdaMEM 2606.05684, EvoMemBench 2605.18421, MemReread 2605.10268, LenVM 2604.27039, 2512.02543; nothing on reader length as a function of item length. (b) 'in-context demonstrations length imitate suboptimal exemplar LLM agent copies number of steps' (unrestricted) -> ICAL 2406.14596, Synapse 2306.07863, Synatra 2409.15637, PositionID 2410.07035, MimicGen 2310.17596; length-control and exemplar-prompting work, no agentic length inheritance. (c) 'raw trajectories versus distilled skills agent memory reuse benchmark' --recent (closest named method) -> SkillEvolBench 2605.24117 (verified), 2608.07169, 2606.23127 (Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents: skill transfer across roles and models), SkillGenBench 2605.18693, SkillCraft 2603.00718; none matches per-reader token cost to gain. (d) 'gain per token cost-matched evaluation of retrieved experience consumer inference overhead agent' --recent -> EMPTY, reported as empty, not as evidence of novelty. (e) 'exemplar trajectory quality affects agent efficiency number of steps ALFWorld retrieval few-shot' --recent -> PANDO 2605.24785 (web agent that accumulates experience specifically to reduce redundant actions -- the intervention half of the proposal's story as a method paper, worth citing), StepOPSD 2605.27140, 2505.00234. (f) 'pruning redundant steps from stored experience reduces agent inference cost without hurting success' --recent -> only chain-of-thought compression work (SWAP 2603.00296, Step Pruner 2510.03805, ConMax 2601.04973, 2608.08389), nothing on stored experience for a foreign reader. Where the proposal's check is thin: it searched agent/memory/RL-length vocabulary but never the vocabulary the mechanism actually lives in for plain LLMs -- exemplar-induced length copying / verbosity imitation in in-context learning, which its own novelty card gestures at (2310.05199 length bias, 2406.17744 length constraints, 2410.07035). If few-shot readers are already documented to copy exemplar length in text generation, the agentic version is a transposition rather than a discovery, and the proposal owes reviewers that paragraph. It also does not surface 2607.10608, which is the nearest framing competitor and appeared on the automated novelty card the proposal was shown. Novelty scored on what I verified: mechanism unclaimed, framing partly taken, surprise low.
